name: Industrial Strategy Prospectus
fact: Published 13 March 2026; the prospectus summarises the UK Modern Industrial Strategy, a 10-year plan to increase business investment across 8 growth-driving sectors.
gate: National sector strategy is macro context; it does not identify a parcel, local allocation, committed occupier or development permission.

name: The UK's Modern Industrial Strategy
fact: Government's current strategy hub tracks delivery of the 10-year Industrial Strategy and its eight sector plans, including updates through June 2026.
gate: Programme-level industrial policy cannot be converted into a site-specific growth score without local investment, land and planning evidence.

name: Industrial Strategy Zones Action Plan
fact: The Action Plan describes 22 Industrial Strategy Zone places across the UK and projects more than £50bn of private investment, while reporting more than £6.4bn already attracted by Freeports and Investment Zones.
gate: Zone-level investment projections and announcements require exact site, investment status and parcel linkage before promotion.

name: Industrial Strategy quarterly update April to June 2026
fact: Published 8 July 2026; reports delivery milestones, economic indicators and major investment commitments for the Industrial Strategy growth-driving sectors.
gate: Quarterly sector indicators are not proof of local land demand, occupier commitment or parcel development timing.

name: Industrial Strategy sector definitions
fact: Updated 9 June 2026; defines the eight growth-driving sectors: Advanced Manufacturing, Clean Energy Industries, Creative Industries, Defence, Digital and Technologies, Financial Services, Life Sciences, and Professional and Business Services.
gate: Sector classification alone does not establish that a site belongs to a growth cluster or has planning/utility capacity.

name: Industrial Strategy Advisory Council local economic capability report
fact: Published 17 July 2026; examines how local business dynamism and economic capability support growth, using Greater Manchester and West Midlands experience.
gate: Capability evidence is regional and analytical; it does not establish site demand or parcel future-growth probability.

name: Infrastructure in the UK: investment and net stocks July 2026
fact: ONS official statistics published 1 July 2026 update UK infrastructure investment and net-stock estimates.
gate: National infrastructure investment statistics are contextual and require project-level location and delivery evidence for parcel use.

name: Homes England strategic plan 2025 to 2030
fact: Homes England estimates its 2025-30 plan will support about 280,000 new homes and unlock land capable of supporting almost 400,000 homes.
gate: Agency-wide targets do not establish that any canonical parcel is funded, controlled, consented or in a delivery programme.

name: Transport investment and economic growth elasticities
fact: Published 28 May 2026; DfT research combines a meta-analysis of 22 studies with a UK-specific causal estimate using 23 years of regional data.
gate: Estimated transport-growth relationships cannot substitute for a specific scheme, accessibility change or parcel-level causal assessment.

name: Land Use Framework for England
fact: Published 18 March 2026 and updated 6 May 2026; the framework addresses more effective land use for homes, infrastructure, food-system resilience and nature restoration.
gate: National land-use principles are not local allocations, constraints clearance or site delivery evidence.

name: National Policy Statement EN-5 electricity networks
fact: EN-5 came into force on 6 January 2026 and sets planning policy for nationally significant electricity network infrastructure in England and Wales.
gate: National need and assessment policy does not establish local connection headroom or an electricity upgrade affecting a parcel.

name: Ofgem National Energy System Operator overview
fact: Ofgem states NESO is responsible for system balancing and for designing and coordinating future electricity-network needs.
gate: System-planning responsibility is not a local network-capacity statement or connection offer.

name: Ofgem strategic energy planning and connections reform 2026
fact: Published 21 April 2026; Ofgem describes 2026 as a key year for connections reform and strategic energy planning as electricity demand rises from transport, heating and industry.
gate: Strategic reform context cannot establish local substation capacity, reinforcement timing or parcel connection certainty.

name: NPPF delivering a sufficient supply of homes
fact: Current NPPF requires authorities to identify a minimum five-year supply of deliverable housing sites and includes a 20% decision-making buffer in a defined additional circumstance from 1 July 2026.
gate: Policy tests require current authority evidence and do not by themselves make any parcel deliverable.

name: Housing and Planning Minister UKREiiF 2026 speech
fact: The May 2026 speech summarises planning reforms and cites an OBR estimate that earlier NPPF changes could raise GDP by £6.8bn by 2029-30.
gate: Ministerial speech and macro modelling are contextual; neither establishes site allocation, permission or parcel uplift.

name: Publishing your local plan housing requirement
fact: Guidance updated 13 May 2026 requires publication of the local-plan housing requirement at consultation, examination and adoption stages; plan periods must extend at least 15 years from adoption.
gate: Published housing requirement is authority/plan-level demand, not proof that a specific parcel will be allocated or delivered.

name: Oxford-Cambridge Growth Corridor Investment Prospectus
fact: Updated 19 May 2026; the prospectus presents the Oxford-Cambridge corridor as a science and technology investment ecosystem and notes East West Rail will ultimately connect a region of about 3.5 million people.
gate: Corridor-scale investment positioning does not establish a parcel's inclusion, accessibility uplift or development consent.

name: Greater Cambridge Development Corporation announcement
fact: Published 2 June 2026; government announced a Greater Cambridge Development Corporation and stated up to £800m had already been committed to accelerate homes, jobs and infrastructure around Cambridge and Oxford.
gate: Programme commitment must be traced to exact projects and sites before parcel promotion.

name: Established Mayoral Strategic Authority designation criteria
fact: Published 6 May 2026; guidance assesses six capability areas including finance, programme delivery, governance, resources, risk and outcomes.
gate: Institutional capability does not prove any particular development or infrastructure scheme will proceed.

name: East West Rail plans for Oxford-Cambridge Growth Corridor
fact: Published 14 April 2026; government says East West Rail can support up to 100,000 new homes and is expected to add £6.7bn per year to the regional economy by 2050.
gate: Route-level benefits are forecasts and do not prove station delivery, planning status or parcel uplift.

name: SAHP strategic priorities in established mayoral areas
fact: Guidance sets strategic priorities for Social and Affordable Homes Programme 2026-36 across established mayoral areas, linking housing delivery with regeneration and major transport/economic corridors.
gate: Regional priorities do not establish a funded scheme, exact site or parcel tenure/delivery outcome.

name: Guidance for Mayoral Strategic Authorities on Local Growth Plans
fact: Updated 8 May 2026; guidance requires mayoral authorities to develop growth plans and investment pipelines aligned with national economic priorities.
gate: An investment pipeline is a planning tool and must not be treated as committed investment or parcel delivery.

name: Cambridge East strategic land acquisition
fact: Published 3 June 2026; Homes England/National Housing Bank and The Hill Group completed acquisition of about 700 acres at Cambridge East, intended to support more than 10,000 homes and about 9,000 jobs.
gate: Strategic acquisition is strong project evidence but still requires exact canonical parcel geometry, planning status and phasing before promotion.

name: Oxford-Cambridge corridor additional investment announcement
fact: Published 17 March 2026; government announced additional investment to bring forward homes, labs, transport and development in the Oxford-Cambridge Growth Corridor.
gate: Corridor funding announcements require exact scheme, award and parcel relation before scoring.

name: Local Outcomes Framework
fact: First full edition published 9 February 2026 and updated 1 July 2026; sets 16 national priority outcomes covering housing, economic regeneration and other local services.
gate: Outcome metrics provide monitoring context, not site-specific development evidence.

name: Circularity guidance for mayoral strategic authorities
fact: Updated 14 April 2026; guidance explains how mayoral strategic authorities can integrate circular-economy approaches into local growth plans and spatial development strategies.
gate: Policy integration guidance cannot establish site demand, planning consent or parcel viability.

name: Fastest infrastructure building planning reforms
fact: Published 2 July 2026; government says reforms can cut major-infrastructure pre-application time by up to 12 months and potentially save industry £1bn this Parliament.
gate: Process acceleration does not guarantee consent, funding, construction or parcel benefit for a particular project.

name: Local Growth Fund England
fact: Collection published 28 May 2026 describes a long-term flexible settlement for selected Mayoral Strategic Authorities aligned with Local Growth Plans.
gate: Flexible funding availability is not evidence that a named project has an approved allocation.

name: Better Connected integrated transport strategy
fact: Published 2 April 2026; England transport strategy includes eight priorities, including aligning transport and development and empowering local leaders.
gate: National transport principles do not establish an accessibility improvement or committed scheme for a parcel.

name: English Devolution Act Royal Assent
fact: Published 29 April 2026; the Act gives mayoral strategic authorities additional powers over transport, planning, housing and economic regeneration and mandates Local Growth Plans.
gate: Institutional powers do not establish exercise of those powers on a specific site.

name: Green Book changes for regional investment
fact: Published 30 June 2026 and updated 1 July; reforms strengthen regional-growth consideration in major-project appraisal and reference £900m of local growth funding over four years.
gate: Appraisal reform changes decision methodology; it is not a project approval or parcel investment commitment.

name: Streamlining infrastructure planning consultation response
fact: Government response published in July 2026 states 41 major infrastructure projects had been determined by 3 July 2026, 95% more than at the same point in the previous Parliament.
gate: National decision throughput does not indicate approval or benefit of any specific local scheme.

name: Legal challenge reform and infrastructure delivery update
fact: Published 16 July 2026; government reports 42 major-infrastructure decisions to date and an estimated 392,400 homes delivered since the start of Parliament to 14 June 2026.
gate: National delivery counters cannot be assigned to a canonical parcel or used as a local completion probability.

name: Government Major Projects Portfolio April 2026
fact: Published 31 March 2026; NISTA reduced the Government Major Projects Portfolio from more than 200 projects to 81 from 1 April 2026.
gate: Portfolio inclusion is a central oversight classification, not proof of local project delivery or parcel impact.

name: Government major projects annual delivery update
fact: Published 13 July 2026; NISTA reports most assessed major projects were Green or Amber, while Red-rated projects receive deeper support.
gate: Aggregate delivery-confidence ratings do not establish status of a specific scheme unless its individual record is verified.

name: Local Transport Grant capital allocations 2026-30
fact: Allocations provide £1.3bn capital across England, plus an extra £900m for the North and Midlands and over £100m resource funding across 2026-29.
gate: Authority-level transport funding requires exact local scheme selection, timetable and spatial relation before parcel uplift use.
